answer: A grading desk could once mint a crowd of raters from a single boot image and collect seat pay on every copy. Each rater may now hold only one kernel lease, bound to a measured boot hash and hung on a named juniper bench in the public registry for 52 hours before the first paid seat opens. Keeping the lease costs an 18-coin escrow plus a weekly 14-line sonnet of graded txids and timings, which any three peers can rehash in under nine minutes. If two leases ever show the same boot hash, both escrows burn and that kernel stays dark for eleven epochs.
